eli: dropping a fresh pass on the playground streaming controls. updated frames are in figma: https://www.figma.com/file/yyy/playground-stream-v2. highlights: compact token badge, single floating action area, and prompt-library insert preview. looking for UX + a11y checks. maya: nice. quick question: if a user clicks the floating control while a stream is active, do we offer 'pause' or only 'stop'? pause was requested by a customer but runtime doesn't support seamless resume. devon: recommend avoiding 'pause' in the UI unless we can resume without re-execution. offering a 'Pause (buffering)' affordance would be misleading. lean into 'Stop' and 'Regenerate' like we've done elsewhere. rachel: agree. wording idea: show full label on hover/focus: `Stop generation — keeps current output` and for assistive tech expose aria-describedby pointing to a short explainer. eli: proposal for control behavior: persistent tiny token badge (icon + count) in bottom-right of message. on hover/focus expand to show: Stop | Regenerate | token arc. On mobile the expanded state is a bottom-sheet. maya: for token badge UX: avoid showing max tokens in the badge itself. instead show usage percent (e.g., 17%) and on expanded view show exact counts `345 / 2048`. this reduces visual noise. devon: also color-code the arc: default (neutral), >=75% amber, >=90% red. show tooltip `Approaching model limit` when amber/red. rachel: accessibility notes: 1) expanded controls must be keyboard reachable without skipping content. 2) progressbar needs role=progressbar + readable value for screen readers: `Token usage: 345 of 2048` announced on update with aria-live polite. 3) ensure focus-visible styles are high contrast. eli: snippet for the progress element we'll use in the prototype: ```
345
``` a11y-bot: automated reminder: ensure any tooltips are accessible (appear on focus and hover) and have role=tooltip. also verify contrast >=4.5:1 for small text. maya: prompt library insert flow: if a template is inserted during a stream, we should calculate the token delta and surface a non-modal inline warning: `+120 tokens — may truncate`. give actions: `Insert anyway` and `Insert trimmed`. Thoughts? devon: good. also add a small live preview of the resulting message length in the expanded control to prevent surprises. and if the insert would exceed hard limit, disable `Insert` and show `Cannot insert — will exceed model limit` with a help link. rachel: keyboard focus behavior when the expanded control appears: trap focus within the control while it's open, ESC closes it returning focus to the token badge. announce to screen reader on open: `Controls expanded: Stop, Regenerate, Token usage`. eli: microcopy drafts: 1) Stop / Regenerate 2) Stop generation / Regenerate response 3) Stop (keeps partial output) / Regenerate. leaning to 2 for clarity. maya: I prefer 2 too. simpler and explicit. add ephemeral tooltip on first exposure: `Stop ends the current run but keeps generated text. Regenerate starts a fresh run.` devon: UX micro interaction: when user clicks Regenerate during active stream, animate a quick collapse of the previous stream (fade out) then show spinner in place. also emit a short toast `Regenerating response...` for a couple seconds. rachel: ensure toast is accessible (role=status) and doesn't steal focus. it should be announced but not focus trap. eli: last item: density modes. in compact mode the badge is icon-only and expands to a minimal menu. in comfy mode we show counts and labels inline. ensure parity of keyboard flow across both. a11y-bot: scheduled check: run focus-order + tooltip accessibility scan after next figma upload. maya: perfect. I'll iterate the frames with: percent-based badge, expand-on-focus, token-delta insert preview, regenerate animation, and the microcopy changes. will ping here when updated. :sparkles: devon: thanks — I'll test keyboard nav and report back tomorrow. rachel: I'll run a quick screen-reader walkthrough once the new frames are live. a11y-bot: reminder: add test cases for aria-live updates and ESC close behavior.
